title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Playbook (Q2 2026)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s core Finance & Legal operating procedures for budgeting & forecasting, contracts and legal process, procurement and vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for finance managers, legal counsel, procurement agents, product finance partners, and department owners.

Scope:
- Applies to all corporate and product teams that incur spend, sign contracts, or generate revenue for Redwood Inference (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Covers annual and quarterly budgeting, procurement thresholds and approvals, contract lifecycle steps for customer and vendor contracts, and revenue recognition/billing rules used by RevRec & Billing.

Primary goals:
1) Establish clear approval paths and SLAs so purchase and contracting activity do not block product delivery.
2) Ensure consistent, GAAP-aligned revenue recognition and timely billing.
3) Minimize procurement cycle time while preserving vendor / legal risk controls.

Roles and ownership:
- Finance (Budget Owners): maintain department budgets, perform forecasts, approve spend above manager-level thresholds.
- Legal: review and sign-off on non-standard contract terms, NDAs, and high-risk vendor agreements.
- Procurement (Proc Ops): execute purchase orders (POs), vendor onboarding, and manage preferred vendor list.
- Product/Engineering Managers: submit procurement requests and provide business justification / cost-center codes.
- Sales & RevOps: manage customer contracts, pricing schedules, invoicing exceptions, and collections escalations.

I. Budgeting & Forecasting

A. Annual Budgeting process (timeline)
1. Oct – Nov: Guidance published by FP&A (headcount targets, capacity planning assumptions, macro scenarios).
2. Nov – Dec: Dept-level draft budgets submitted via Finance budget portal. Include headcount, run-rate cloud/GPU, third-party SaaS, and capital requests.
3. Jan: Consolidation, executive review, and final budget approval.
4. Throughout year: Quarterly re-forecast windows aligned with quarter close (Q1, Q2, Q3).

B. Forecast cadence and artifacts
- Owners must provide a 12-month rolling forecast with monthly granularity.
- Required attachments for material changes (>10% variance): impact analysis, mitigation plan, and owner sign-off.
- Key assumptions: GPU fleet capacity (utilization %), hosted API growth (MAU and token volume), average contract size for Dedicated customers.

C. Budget change & exception process
- Manager-level approvals (<= $25k): direct approval in the budget system.
- Director-level approvals ($25k - $250k): written justification + FP&A review.
- VP/Executive approvals (> $250k): executive finance review and CEO notification for > $1M.
- Material scope changes (new product lines, geographic expansion, or >15% shift) require a Budget Amendment form and CFO approval.

II. Contracts & Legal Process

A. Contract lifecycle (standard flow)
1. Request: Initiated by Sales or Procurement via Contract Request form. Include scope, counterparty legal entity, commercial terms, start/end dates, and risk flags.
2. Draft: Use approved templates (Customer SaaS Agreement, Dedicated Hosting Agreement, NDA, Master Services Agreement).
3. Review: Legal reviews non-standard clauses (data residency, indemnities, IP, liability caps).
4. Commercial approval: Sales/Finance confirm pricing, discounts, and revenue accounting treatment.
5. Signature: Use DocuSign; require signature authority check (see Signing Authority table below).
6. Post-execution: Contracts uploaded to Contract Repository (SharePoint/ContractDB) and referenced by contract ID in billing and CRM.

B. Standard templates and deviation policy
- Use the latest vetted templates (links available in Related Pages). Any deviations from standard terms require Legal approval and must be logged in the Contract Deviation Log.
- High-risk deviations (e.g., unlimited liability, broad data use rights) are escalated to Head of Legal and CFO.

C. Signing authority (summary)
- Individual Contributor: No signature authority.
- Manager: Up to $50k with written pre-approval by Finance.
- Director: Up to $250k.
- VP: Up to $1M.
- CEO/CFO: > $1M or multi-year commitments with significant strategic impact.

III. Procurement & Vendor Onboarding

A. Purchasing thresholds & approvals
- Low value (<= $5k): Manager approval; card transaction acceptable.
- Mid value ($5k - $50k): Manager + Procurement approval; PO recommended.
- High value (>$50k): Procurement + Finance (FP&A) approval; PO required; Legal review if contract present.
- Capital expenditures require CAPEX request forms and capital coding at PO creation.

B. Preferred vendor list and sole-source justification
- Procurement maintains a preferred vendor list for recurring categories (cloud providers, data providers, GPU vendors, professional services).
- Sole-source purchases > $50k require written justification, market scan, and Procurement Director sign-off.

C. Vendor onboarding checklist (Proc Ops uses a 7-step checklist)
1. Vendor information and W-9 / tax forms collected.
2. Security questionnaire completed if vendor accesses customer or sensitive data.
3. Insurance certificates verified for material vendors (limits: $2M general liability standard).
4. Contract terms reviewed (scope, SLA, termination, data handling) by Legal.
5. PO created and approved by Finance.
6. Vendor added to AP system with payment terms (Net30 default).
7. First payment routed through accounts payable only after PO and contract are in place.

IV. Revenue Recognition & Billing

A. Revenue recognition principles (high-level)
- Redwood follows ASC 606 principles: identify contract(s), identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to performance obligations, and recognize revenue when obligations are satisfied.
- Standard product lines: Hosted API (metered tokens), Dedicated (capacity/term), Private (license + deployment services), Professional services (one-time implementation).

B. Typical recognition patterns
- Hosted API (metered): Recognize revenue in the period tokens are consumed. For prepaid credits or committed-volume contracts, defer recognition and recognize as usage occurs or ratably over the committed period if unused.
- Dedicated (term-based): Recognize ratably over the contract term for capacity and subscription fees. One-time onboarding fees recognized upon delivery of onboarding services if distinct.
- Private (license): Perpetual licensing recognized based on transfer of license if the license is distinct; or ratably over the service period if bundled with ongoing obligations.
- Professional services: Recognize on completion of milestones if milestones are distinct and have standalone value; otherwise use percent-complete.

C. Billing cadence and invoice policies
- Standard billing: Monthly in arrears for metered usage (Hosted API). Invoices issued by the 5th business day following month-end.
- Subscription billing: Monthly or annual, billed in advance. Refunds handled per the customer contract (see Refund & Credit policy).
- Payment terms: Net30 default; exceptions require Finance approval.
- Taxes: Sales tax / VAT applied per customer locale. RevOps ensures tax treatment is validated for cross-border customers.

D. Credit memos, refunds, and disputes
- Dispute window: Customers have 60 days from invoice date to dispute charges. Disputes routed to RevOps and Sales for resolution; Finance issues credit memos when validated.
- Refunds are exceptional and require Revenue Manager + Finance Director sign-off; record reason and accounting entries.

E. Revenue cutover for multi-element arrangements
- When contracts include multiple deliverables (e.g., Dedicated capacity + professional services + support), allocate transaction price to performance obligations using standalone selling price hierarchy. Document allocation schedule in the contract file and RevRec workbook.

V. Controls, reporting, and SLAs

A. Control requirements
- All POs must be created prior to invoice payment; exceptions must be escalated and documented.
- All executed customer contracts must be in Contract Repository with contract ID linked to CRM opportunity and billing account.
- Monthly close: Revenue and deferred revenue reconciliations performed by Revenue Accounting; FP&A performs variance analysis on forecast vs actual.

B. Reporting and dashboards
- Finance publishes a monthly Revenue Dashboard (run rate MRR, ARR, deferred revenue, churn) and a Spend Dashboard (category-level spend, top vendors, committed vs actual).
- Procurement provides a quarterly Supplier Performance report (on-time delivery, contract compliance, security posture).

C. SLA for transactional requests
- Contract turn-around: Standard NDA or Template SOW review within 3 business days. Non-standard contract review target within 7-10 business days.
- PO processing: Standard PO creation within 2 business days of an approved requisition.
- Vendor onboarding: Target 7 business days for low-risk vendors, 15-30 days for vendors requiring security review.

VI. Operational checklists and forms (quick reference)

A. Contract Request minimum fields:
- Requester name, business justification, counterparty legal entity, contract template to use, commercial terms summary, requested signature deadline.

B. Purchase Requisition minimum fields:
- Cost center, GL code, vendor, estimated amount, business justification, requested delivery date, requester manager approval.

C. Revenue close checklist (monthly)
- Verify invoice postings and AR aging, reconcile deferred revenue, review revenue adjustments > 2% of month revenue, sign-off by Revenue Manager.

Appendices

Appendix A — Approval & Threshold Table:
- Card spend: <= $5k (Manager)
- PO recommended: $5k–$50k (Manager + Procurement)
- PO required: > $50k (Procurement + Finance)
- Contract signature: Director up to $250k; VP up to $1M; CEO/CFO > $1M

Appendix B — Common GL Codes (examples):
- 5000: Hosting & Cloud (Opex)
- 5100: GPU Fleet (Opex)
- 5200: Professional Services (Opex)
- 4000: Hosted API Revenue
- 4100: Dedicated Revenue (Subscription)

Appendix C — Useful links and templates:
- Contract templates: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/templates
- Budget portal: finance.redwood.internal/budget-portal
- PO form: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/po-request-form
